headline: Medium risk: shared-file workflows can create prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors; no direct write conflict is exposed.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and validate files, and Marker processes document content; if Marker output is copied into Great Expectations inputs or shared files, instruction-like text could be misread. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from file-based workflows rather than proven interaction.
conditions: IF Marker output is manually copied into files that Great Expectations later parses as trusted content
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents
Strip instructions from document text before handing it to Great Expectations
Add a human review step before any file is reused across agents
Use provenance labels on intermediate files
requires-engineering: add parser hardening for untrusted file content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Marker touches no data classes in the profile and has no filesystem read/write capability listed. With no shared workspace or egress shown, leakage is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to manual file sharing.
conditions: IF the operator manually places sensitive files into a shared folder both agents can access
IF Marker is run in an environment where its undocumented data handling exceeds the profile
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Run Marker on non-sensitive samples first
Verify both agents' working directories are isolated
Delete intermediate artifacts after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, but Marker is explicitly unable to write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, or install packages. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable capabilities, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF Marker is deployed with capabilities beyond the profile
IF Great Expectations is embedded in an orchestrator that grants both agents the same writable directory
mitigations: Avoid giving Great Expectations shared write access
Document any capability changes before pairing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker can transform documents, and Great Expectations can validate resulting files; if Great Expectations consumes Marker output as authoritative input, errors can cascade into incorrect validation or downstream decisions. No verification or critique loop is documented in either profile, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes Marker-produced text without a verification step
IF the operator treats validation results as authoritative after a single pass
mitigations: Insert a manual verification step between agents
Compare Marker output against source documents before validation
Use a checksum or diff on intermediate files

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. Great Expectations lists documentation and validation artifacts; Marker lists no touched data classes. With no cited compliance gap, there is no evidenced compliance risk in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints not present in the profiles
mitigations: Review retention settings if regulated data is introduced
Keep regulated workloads out of this pair unless policies are documented
